item.title: Nepal floods swept ​bodies 200km downstream, 3 found in UP
item.description: A significant collapse in the Himalayan region caused a seismic disturbance, leading to a violent flood surge that reached Rasuwagadhi at the Nepal-Tibet border within a mere seven minutes. Recovery efforts extended across multiple districts in both Nepal and India. Alarmingly, Nepal’s flood authorities were only informed after the surge had already impacted Bhote Koshi. In response, SMS warnings were promptly issued to those residing along the riverbanks.
item.dc:creator: VISHANT AGARWALA

item.title: Asia Cup: Anything less than title will be a 'major disappointment' for India
item.description: Given the historic dominance of the Indian team in the tournament, former India cricketer and ex-women's team coach WV Raman believes anything less than a title in the upcoming 2026 Women's Asia Cup would be a "major disappointment" for Harmanpreet Kaur's team.
item.dc:creator: SHUBHANSHU DWIVEDI

item.title: Delhi-Meerut Expressway crawls for hours as Raksha Bandhan traffic hits NCR
item.description: Raksha Bandhan travel caused significant traffic delays across Noida and Ghaziabad. Commuters faced hours of congestion on major roads and expressways. Heavy pressure on roads intensified due to thousands traveling to hometowns. Rain spells further worsened the already difficult traffic situation. Festive rush continued, impacting key routes connecting Delhi-NCR with western Uttar Pradesh.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: US govt planning new tariffs on imported chips, tech leaders warn of AI setback
item.description: The Trump administration is exploring potential tariffs on imported semiconductors, which might raise prices for various devices, including laptops and gaming consoles. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick supports a proposal that connects tariff relief with foreign investment. However, technology leaders caution that this strategy could threaten the U.S. leadership in artificial intelligence and raise consumer costs, as the administration aims to bolster domestic chip manufacturing while maintaining national security.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Who are India's NEET youth? What NITI's 8.7 crore figure really tells us
item.description: A NITI Aayog report identifies significant barriers to youth employment and skilling in India. Existing skilling programs often lack outcome orientation and placement support for participants. The report suggests affordable training and combining learning with earning opportunities. Bridging this gap is very important for realizing India's demographic dividend by 2047.
item.dc:creator: ARGHYA PRASUN ROYCHOWDHURY

item.title: Trump changes Lake Ontario’s name to ‘Lake America’ amid tensions with Canada
item.description: Trump signed an executive order on Thursday changing the lake's name for the US geographic naming service. The decision applies to how the body of water is officially identified by US authorities, but Trump has no power to make Canada adopt the new name. The move follows Trump's earlier decision to rename the Gulf of Mexico as the “Gulf of America” for use by the US government.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: 75+ Raksha Bandhan messages, wishes and quotes
item.description: Raksha Bandhan is a vibrant celebration of the special bond shared between siblings. This cherished festival highlights the unbreakable ties between brothers and sisters, encouraging the sharing of heartfelt, humorous, or succinct messages that resonate with familial love. The article curates a variety of engaging greetings and status suggestions for Raksha Bandhan, aimed at fostering deeper connections and creating fond memories among loved ones.
item.dc:creator: TOI TRENDING DESK

item.title: A Hawaii retreat, staff revolt, and weak AI: How Meta's 60% layoffs plan came apart
item.description: Meta explored cutting some teams by up to 60% and handing their work to AI agents under a plan code-named Project OT. Hatched at Mark Zuckerberg's Hawaii retreat, it involved two layoff waves, pods of three replacing traditional teams, and keystroke tracking to train AI models. Staff revolted, internal sentiment fell from 74% to 55%, and Meta's own data showed the AI wasn't delivering promised productivity gains.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: How software engineer wanted for Hyderabad techie’s US murder was traced to Agra
item.description: A fugitive software engineer wanted for murder in Maryland was arrested in Agra. Arjun Sharma was apprehended by Telangana Police following an Interpol Red Corner Notice. He allegedly killed Nikitha Godishala on December 31, 2025, over a monetary dispute. A Delhi court has now cleared the way for his extradition proceedings to the US. The arrest followed a cheating case registered by the victim's family in India.
item.dc:creator: SUDEEP LAVANIA AND MAHESH BUDDI

item.title: Kerala bus overturns at petrol pump after driver swerves to avoid two-wheeler, 20 injured
item.description: A tourist bus carrying wedding guests overturned near a petrol pump in Kakkoor. The vehicle swerved to avoid a two-wheeler, losing control and crashing. Around twenty passengers sustained injuries and were taken to local hospitals. Fortunately, no serious injuries were reported from the incident. Police are investigating the accident and reviewing CCTV footage.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: In 1984, Nasa sent 3,301 bees to space to see how they built honeycomb
item.description: Thousands of honeybees travelled into space aboard NASA's Space Shuttle Discovery in 1984. These bees survived microgravity and adapted to their new environment within days. The mission aimed to observe bee behavior and compare space-built honeycomb. The bees successfully built approximately 200 cm of honeycomb during the seven-day mission. Researchers noted differences in cell diameter and wall thickness compared to Earth-made structures.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Glacier sheared off, plunged 1.2km before ‘liquid concrete’ flood swamped Nepal
item.description: Satellite images analysed by Isro’s national remote sensing centre showed that almost two-thirds of the glacier body had detached. A Sentinel-2 image from Aug 24 showed the glacier intact, while a Landsat-9 image taken after the disaster on Aug 26 revealed a large scar identified as the “zone of glacier breakage and collapse”. The images also traced a broad ice-rock avalanche path descending towards the river.
item.dc:creator: VISHANT AGARWALA

item.title: Delhi model murder: Prime accused Imran arrested after encounter
item.description: Police apprehended Imran, a suspect in Muskan's murder, after a manhunt across three states. The accused sustained a gunshot injury during his arrest and is now receiving hospital treatment. Imran allegedly attacked Muskan with a knife after an argument broke out at her home. He had previously harassed and stalked the victim, and the murder is believed to be pre-planned.
item.dc:creator: ABHAY

item.title: PCB threatens player protest after Atherton’s interview with Imran Khan’s sons
item.description: The Pakistan Cricket Board objected to Sky Sports airing an interview with Imran Khan's sons. The interview focused on their father's health and safety concerns while imprisoned. Sky Sports initially delayed the broadcast before showing it during the lunch interval. Khan's sons discussed their father's medical condition and access to treatment. This controversy arose after a Supreme Court order regarding Khan's hospital admission.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: 'Will send Netanyahu to hell’: Iran warns of ‘confrontation’ if US blockade continues
item.dc:creator: VIVEK DUBEY

item.title: Toxic box office day 2: Yash's film sees drop, earns Rs 36 crore
item.description: Yash's latest release 'Toxic' made an impressive debut, raking in over one hundred crore rupees on its opening day. However, Thursday saw a dip in earnings, generating only thirty-six point four zero crore net. With the upcoming weekend and Raksha Bandhan holiday on the horizon, foot traffic is expected to increase.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: PM Modi on 4-day visit to Uzbekistan, Kyrgyz Republic - what's on agenda
item.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic from August 29 to September 1. He will hold talks in Tashkent to strengthen bilateral ties and explore new economic opportunities. Discussions will cover trade, critical minerals, and healthcare cooperation between the nations. In Bishkek, he will attend the SCO Summit and highlight India's priorities. The visit also includes the opening ceremony of the World Nomad Games.
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: Praggnanandhaa scripts history, becomes first Indian to win Grand Chess Tour
item.description: In a remarkable display of skill and tenacity, R Praggnanandhaa clinched victory at the Grand Chess Tour Finals in St. Louis, overturning a daunting six-point deficit against renowned competitor Fabiano Caruana. This landmark win not only made him the first Indian champion of the Grand Chess Tour but also earned him a hefty prize of $200,000, solidifying his status in the chess world.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Sensex dives 2,200 points in 5 mins, recovers 2,000 points in next 7
item.description: On Thursday, within a five-minute window after the start of CAS on BSE—between 3.18pm and 3.23pm—sensex crashed over 2,200 points and then within the next seven minutes—between 3.23pm and 3.30pm—it recovered nearly 2,000 points. It finally closed at 76,934 points, down 539 points from its Wednesday close. On NSE, things were relatively quiet. Between 3.18pm and 3.22pm, Nifty slid over 100 points.
item.dc:creator: PARTHA SINHA

item.title: Ronaldo cries 'intensely' after being substituted on Al-Nassr comeback; here's why
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo reportedly requested to be substituted at half-time during Al-Nassr’s 3-2 comeback win over Al-Ettifaq, with Saudi journalist Khalid Al-Shanif claiming the star was “crying intensely” afterward. Ange Postecoglou said Ronaldo was always scheduled to play 45 minutes as his fitness is managed. Ronaldo then watched from the bench as Al-Nassr overturned a two-goal deficit.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Oklahoma woman's $1,373 power bill tops rent, sparks petition over soaring costs
item.description: As intense summer heat sweeps through the region, many households are grappling with skyrocketing electricity bills. Raelynn McMurchy's monthly statement doubled, igniting discussions on much-needed policy reforms. Oklahoma's power provider continues to disconnect customers in alarming numbers, leaving local charities to struggle for emergency support. Residents are calling for robust measures to prevent power shutoffs during the scorching months.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Anthropic tells employees at its San Francisco office to work from home
item.description: Anthropic asked its employees to work remotely this week due to a potential security guard walkout. The security contractor, Allied Universal, had warned the AI company about this possibility. However, the guards' union stated that no strike authorization vote has occurred. This action by Anthropic appears to be a precautionary measure against an unconfirmed threat. The company is preparing for a potential initial public offering soon.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: BPCL CMD says mulling E10 petrol option, then walks back
item.description: “We are looking into various related aspects but nothing has been finalised yet,” said the chief of the oil marketing company that is the leading coordinator for the ethanol blending programme. However, a few hours later, amid growing scrutiny, he claimed that he had been misquoted. “His response is being misquoted to suggest as if E10 is being considered as an option, which is not correct, it said.
item.dc:creator: ATUL MATHUR

item.title: India expresses readiness for treaty talks with Canada, eyes Rs 4.65 lakh crore trade
item.description: The two ministers discussed ways to strengthen trade and investment ties and agreed on several areas of economic cooperation. "India expressed its readiness to initiate negotiations on a Bilateral Investment Treaty at the earliest," the joint statement issued after the meeting said. A Bilateral Investment Treaty is an agreement between two countries designed to provide greater protection and certainty to investors from both sides.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: Parliament may be reconvened, hints Rijiju, brings delimitation bill in focus
item.description: Though Rijiju made no categorical comment about an immediate session to take up the constitutional amendment bill to implement the law from 2029 with a 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats, he said Parliament has been reconvened in the past after a session was not prorogued. The monsoon session, which ended on Aug 13, has not been prorogued yet.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: ‘Test cricket won’: Shubman Gill after Sri Lanka force draw in Colombo
item.description: Following a thrilling second Test match, India captain Shubman Gill hailed the outcome as a victory after Sri Lanka's determined resistance led to a draw. The Sri Lankan team batted fiercely for 154 overs, earning a hard-fought tie. Gill commended their fighting spirit and particularly noted the potential of spinner Manav Suthar for upcoming Indian squads. This match secured India's series win at 1-0.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: PM Modi to meet Russia's Putin on SCO meeting sidelines
item.description: PM Modi’s bilateral with Putin, the first since the Russian President visited India in Dec 2025 for the annual summit, will follow external affairs minister S Jaishankar’s visit to Moscow this week for a meeting of the 27th India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation during which he also called on Putin.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: 400-year-old Polish grave reveals a young woman buried to prevent her return
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Govt plans to engage third-party auditor to inspect NHs, e-ways
item.description: EIL had earlier carried out the task of third-party quality check during the construction of the Golden Quadrilateral, the country’s first flagship highway development programme under the then PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee. In recent years, increased instances of deficiencies in NH projects have become a cause of concern, as these have attracted criticism from the public.
item.dc:creator: DIPAK K DASH

item.title: Nepal floods: No adverse impact of flash floods on Indian side, says NDRF
item.description: NDRF has deployed 20 teams — 11 in UP and nine in Bihar — for evacuation, relief and rescue operations in case these areas experience floods and waterlogging. These include an NDRF team deployed in Kushinagar district, near Gorakhpur in Uttar Pradesh. In a media briefing, NDRF IG Narendra Bundela said floods have caused massive destruction in Nepal with hundreds of people, including Indian tourists, reported missing.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Join sports, playgrounds more important than PlayStation: PM to youth
item.description: Speaking at the Khelo India dialogue, he said, “More important than screens are sports centres. More important than PlayStation is the playground. And this will happen only when the youth embrace this approach.” Lamenting India’s absence from almost half of Olympic sports, he said that is why he had announced a talent hunt for children in the 5-15 years age bracket.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: HDFC looks to appeal 99.97% haircut on claims against Zee’s Chandra
item.description: Assenting creditors (80.8%) contested allegations of being related parties and argued that Rs. 6.5-crore plan offered a better outcome compared to pushing the personal guarantor into bankruptcy, since Chandra’s net worth according to the resolution professional was only Rs. 31.8 crore, of which Rs. 25 crore was his mortgaged house. Chandra has disputed the Rs. 22,000-crore liability, stating it reflected historical claims filed in 2022.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: OpenAI rolls out ChatGPT ads in India, over 50 brands on board
item.description: From Sept 4, businesses will also get access to a self-serve ChatGPT ads manager, with daily campaign budgets starting at Rs 725, potentially opening the platform to smaller advertisers alongside large brands. An OpenAI spokesperson told TOI that the company expects early advertiser interest across travel, financial services, retail, and health and beauty.
item.dc:creator: AABHAS SHARMA

item.title: BJP cites ‘jhooth ki goonj’ site to hit out at Rahul Gandhi
item.description: “Rahul’s every lie will be countered with facts. The ‘jhooth ki goonj’ website is exposing every lie of his. The louder propaganda echoes, the faster truth will emerge,” BJP spokesperson Anil Banluni said. Party neta Sudhanshu Trivedi said Rahul is full of frustration and envy vis-a-vis PM Modi, but every lie of his is being exposed.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Hours after blocking, X restores account of organisation hosting Bhagwat in New York
item.description: The @AheadForum1 handle of American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue (AHEAD Forum) became unavailable Wednesday, three days before Bhagwat’s address at Madison Square Garden’s Infosys Theatre. Seeking restoration, AHEAD Forun had earlier said that the suspension “may have occurred in error” and its communications promoted “universal peace, oneness, harmony” and interfaith dialogue. No public evidence links X’s action to protests around the programme.
item.dc:creator: MANASH PRATIM GOHAIN

item.title: India’s petroleum products’ exports surge 8% in July
item.description: Govt data showed India exported 2.4 million tonnes (MT) of diesel in July this year, up from 2.2 MT in the corresponding month last year, while total petroleum product exports rose from 5 MT to 5.5 MT. Diesel is currently commanding nearly 70% premium over crude, making exports lucrative for refiners despite the windfall gains tax govt brought in to ensure adequate domestic stocks.
item.dc:creator: ATUL MATHUR

item.title: Supreme Court issues directions to expedite dowry trials
item.description: The bench also directed states/Union territories and high courts to conduct periodic training and sensitisation programmes for judicial officers, police officials, prosecutors, protection officers, counsellors through judicial academies, police training institutions and other appropriate bodies. A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Augustine George Masih said there was a need for time-bound completion of trial in dowry cases and directed the high courts to periodically review pending criminal appeals.
